mainTopic: Virginity claims, a bad reputation and רב פפא's tainted document, and the משנה of girls who get no קנס, including רבי יהודה's view on a redeemed captive
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer about a בוגרת: a 'no blood' claim works against her, but an 'open entrance' claim does not. Next, סומכוס rules that a blind girl has no virginity claim against her. She may have been hurt in a fall without seeing it and telling her mother. רב ששת explains that a girl with a bad reputation from her youth gets no קנס. From this, רב פפא learns that a tainted document cannot collect a debt. The tainted document is one whose owner was caught by two witnesses trying to get it forged. A new משנה then lists girls who get no קנס: a convert, a captive or a maidservant freed after age three, and close relatives whose relations carry a court death penalty. The גמרא discusses רבי יהודה's view that a redeemed captive keeps her status, with רבה and אביי debating whether רבי דוסא truly agrees with him. Two answers, from רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, explain an apparent contradiction in רבי יהודה's rulings about marrying a captive. A new contradiction from רב פפא בר שמואל begins at the very end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A blood claim works, but an open-entrance claim does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that a husband can make a claim against a בוגרת if he says there was no blood. The ברייתא's rule that she has no virginity claim refers only to a claim of 'open entrance.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he claims there was no blood, then yes, he has a valid claim. Here, in the ברייתא, we are dealing with someone who claims he found an 'open entrance.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a challenge to the ברייתא's rule that a בוגרת (adult girl) has no טענת בתולים. It says the rule covers only one type of claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of virginity claims: 'no blood' and 'open entrance.' A 'no blood' claim still works against a בוגרת. An 'open entrance' claim does not, because an adult girl's body is no longer completely closed in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: A claim that there was no blood after the first relations
A claim that he found an 'open entrance' (no intact hymen)
'Indeed so': conceding a point
'Here, what case are we dealing with?': narrowing the case

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא means a בוגרת can never face any virginity claim. The גמרא limits the rule to the 'open entrance' claim only.

phrases.english: If he makes a claim about blood (that there was none),
indeed, so it is (he has a valid claim).
Here, with what are we dealing?
With one who claims he found an 'open entrance.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a challenge from before this section about the בוגרת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say a בוגרת can never face any virginity claim
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the 'open entrance' claim fails against her; a 'no blood' claim works

steps.title: סומכוס: a blind girl has no virginity claim
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: סומכוס, in the name of רבי מאיר, says a blind girl cannot have a virginity claim made against her.
steps.simpleTranslation: סומכוס says in the name of רבי מאיר: A blind girl has no virginity claim.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a new ruling. A husband cannot bring a virginity claim against a blind girl he married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new case on the list of women who are not subject to טענת בתולים. The ruling is stated here without a reason. The גמרא will ask for the reason next.

keyTerms.meaning: A blind person (here, a blind girl)
A husband's claim that his bride was not a virgin

phrases.english: Sumakhos says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
A blind girl has no claim of virginity.
phrases.notes: He means the husband can't bring a virginity complaint against her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next clause of the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband cannot make a virginity claim against a blind girl

steps.title: What is סומכוס's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a blind girl should be different.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of סומכוס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind סומכוס's ruling. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being blind has no obvious connection to virginity. So the גמרא needs to explain why blindness should change the law.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Sumakhos?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a blind girl is not subject to a virginity claim

steps.title: רבי זירא: she may have fallen and been injured
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that a blind girl falls to the ground, and the fall may break her hymen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Because she gets struck by falling onto the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives the reason. A blind girl falls often, and a fall can cause the injury that the husband would complain about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she lost her virginal signs through a fall, she did nothing wrong. So her husband has no real complaint against her.

keyTerms.meaning: She is struck or knocked (by falling)
On the ground

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Because she gets struck by falling onto the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A blind girl falls to the ground, which can break her hymen

steps.title: But all girls fall down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that every girl falls sometimes, so why should a blind girl be different?
steps.simpleTranslation: All girls also get knocked down by falling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's answer. Falling happens to everyone, not just to blind girls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If falling were the whole reason, no girl would ever face a virginity claim. So the reason must include something that only applies to a blind girl.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them (all girls)
They do get knocked down

phrases.english: Don't all girls also get knocked down?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Falling is common to all girls, so it cannot explain a rule that applies only to a blind girl

steps.title: Other girls see it and tell their mothers
steps.stepSummary: A sighted girl sees the bleeding and shows her mother, so the injury becomes known. A blind girl cannot see it, so nobody knows.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the other girls see the blood and show it to their mothers. This blind girl does not see it and does not show it to her mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי זירא. The difference is not the fall itself but whether anyone finds out about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a sighted girl is injured, she shows her mother, so the injury becomes known. A blind girl's injury may stay hidden. So a man who marries a blind girl should have known this could happen, and he cannot complain afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: They see and show
Their mother

steps.whatToRemember: A blind girl has no virginity claim against her because she may have been injured by a fall without knowing it or telling anyone.

phrases.english: All others see the blood and show it to their mother.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ, אֵינָהּ רוֹאָה וְאֵינָהּ מַרְאָה לְאִמָּהּ.
phrases.english: This one does not see and does not show her mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Falling is the same for all girls
steps.terutzMaskana: What matters is whether the injury becomes known, and a blind girl's injury stays hidden

steps.title: A girl who leaves due to a bad reputation gets no fine
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that a girl who 'leaves due to a bad reputation' gets neither the fine for rape nor the fine for seduction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who leaves due to a bad reputation has neither the fine for rape nor the fine for seduction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last line of the ברייתא so it can examine it. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah gives fines (קנס) to a girl who is raped or seduced. This line says a certain girl does not get them. The question is who exactly 'one who leaves due to a bad reputation' is.

keyTerms.meaning: A bad reputation (of sexual misconduct)
The Torah's fine for raping a girl
Seduction, and the fine paid for it

phrases.english: And one who leaves due to a bad reputation

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהּ לֹא קְנָס וְלֹא פִּיתּוּי.
phrases.english: has neither the rape fine nor the seduction fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl who leaves due to a bad reputation gets no fine for rape or seduction

steps.title: She deserves stoning, so of course there is no fine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that if 'leaves due to a bad reputation' means she committed adultery while betrothed, she deserves stoning. Saying she gets no fine would be obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who leaves due to a bad reputation deserves stoning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the plain reading of the line. A betrothed girl caught in adultery is far beyond the question of fines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first, the line sounds like the Torah's case of a betrothed girl found guilty of adultery, whose punishment is סקילה. Telling us that such a girl gets no money would be pointless. So the line must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who deserves death by stoning

phrases.english: One who leaves due to a bad reputation
deserves stoning!
phrases.notes: He's assuming she was caught cheating while betrothed, which carries the death penalty.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיּוֹצֵאת מִשּׁוּם שֵׁם רָע — בַּת סְקִילָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain meaning of the line in step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she is an adulteress who deserves stoning, saying she gets no fine is obvious and pointless

steps.title: רב ששת: a girl with a bad reputation from her youth
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the line refers to a girl who had a reputation for sexual activity when she was young. She is presumed not to be a virgin, so she gets no fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: This is what it means: a girl about whom a bad reputation went out in her youth has neither the rape fine nor the seduction fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת reinterprets the line. It is not about an adulteress at all, but about a young girl who had a bad reputation before anything else happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fines are only paid for a virgin. A girl known for sexual activity since her youth is presumed not to be a virgin. So she loses the fines, even though nobody proved anything in court.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means': reinterpreting a text
In her youth

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'leaves' (יוצאת) as leaving a husband here. רב ששת reads it as a reputation that 'went out' (יצא) about her.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב ששת's reading gives weight to a reputation, and רב פפא will build on that in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיָּצָא עָלֶיהָ שֵׁם רַע בְּיַלְדוּתָהּ —
phrases.english: one about whom a bad reputation went out in her youth

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהּ לֹא קְנָס וְלֹא פִּיתּוּי.
phrases.english: has neither the rape fine nor the seduction fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line is about a betrothed adulteress who deserves stoning
steps.terutzMaskana: The line is about a girl with a bad reputation from her youth, who is presumed not to be a virgin

steps.title: רב פפא: a tainted document cannot collect
steps.stepSummary: From רב ששת's reading, רב פפא concludes that a document with a cloud over it cannot be used to collect a debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Learn from this that we do not collect a debt with a tainted document.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא draws a lesson from רב ששת's reading. A bad reputation cancels a girl's fine, and in the same way a document with a bad 'reputation' cannot be used to collect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא compares a person's reputation to a document's reputation. If a cloud of suspicion takes away the girl's rights, a cloud of suspicion also takes away a document's power. What counts as 'tainted' is still unclear, and the גמרא will ask about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it
A 'weak' or tainted document
We do not collect a debt with it

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Learn from this:
phrases.notes: 'This' is רב ששת's reading from the step before.

phrases.english: this tainted document,
we do not collect a debt with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical lesson from step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tainted document cannot be used to collect a debt

steps.title: What kind of tainted document?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רב פפא means by a 'tainted document.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the circumstances?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks exactly what kind of document רב פפא is talking about. This sets up the suggestions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's comparison only works if the document's case matches the girl's case. So the גמרא needs to find a case that truly matches.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case behind step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of document counts as 'tainted' in רב פפא's statement

steps.title: Not a rumor of forgery, since רבא ignores town rumors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a document rumored to be forged, matching a girl rumored to be promiscuous. It rejects this, because רבא rules that a town rumor about a woman is ignored.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say a rumor went out that the document is forged, then the matching case here is a rumor that she was promiscuous. But didn't רבא say: if a rumor that she was promiscuous went out in town, we are not concerned about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first explanation and knocks it down. A plain rumor cannot be what רב ששת meant, because רבא says rumors like that are ignored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A forgery rumor about a document would match a promiscuity rumor about a girl. But רבא rules that such a rumor does not count against a woman. So רב ששת's 'bad reputation' must be something stronger than a rumor, and the tainted document must be something else too.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)
A rumor
Forged
But didn't (so-and-so) say: introduces a challenge
We are not concerned

steps.confusionAlert: Even though this step rejects the rumor case, רב פפא's rule is not rejected. The גמרא is only searching for the right case to explain it.

phrases.english: If you say a rumor went out about it
that the document is forged,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the letter in round brackets and some don't; either way it reads 'that it is forged.'

phrases.english: then the matching case here
is that a rumor went out about her that she was promiscuous.
But didn't Rava say:
if a reputation of promiscuity went out about her in town,
we are not concerned about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to step 11 and rejects it
steps.kashyaTarget: Explaining the tainted document as one rumored to be forged
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rumor about the document would match a rumor about the girl, but רבא rules that such rumors are ignored, so the comparison cannot hold

steps.title: The tainted document: two witnesses say he asked them to forge
steps.stepSummary: The tainted document is one where two witnesses testify that the lender asked them to forge a document. This matches a girl whom two men say asked them for forbidden relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where two men came and said: 'She asked us to sin with her.' The matching case here is where two men came and said: 'He told us: Forge a document for me.'
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the 'town rumor' idea, the גמרא gives a new definition of רב פפא's tainted document, built to match the girl's bad reputation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rumor is not enough, so the גמרא now uses real testimony from two witnesses. For the girl, two men say she tried to sin with them. For the document, two men say the lender tried to get them to forge. Either way, there is solid proof that the person was trying to do the forbidden thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Two people, meaning two valid witnesses
She asked us, she propositioned us
For something forbidden, here forbidden relations
Forge (a document) for me
The matching case, the one just like it

phrases.english: Rather, it is where two came and said:
She propositioned us for forbidden relations.
phrases.notes: Literally 'to them, she asked them.' The witnesses are talking about themselves.

phrases.english: And the matching case here, with the document:
is where two came and said:
he said to us: 'Forge a document for me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected 'rumor' definition from step 12 with a definition based on two witnesses.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is רב פפא's 'tainted document'? (asked in step 11)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A document whose owner was seen by two witnesses trying to get it forged.

steps.title: The two cases are not really alike
steps.stepSummary: The girl can easily find another willing partner, but most people will not agree to forge. So why assume the document is forged?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense there, because immoral men are common. But here, even if he is known to be looking for a forger, are all Jews known to be forgers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison it just made. It points out a difference between the girl and the document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the girl, even if these two men refused her, we can assume she found someone else, because immoral men are common. With the document, the lender needs someone to forge for him. Most Jews are honest and would refuse, so we should not assume he succeeded.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (in one case), used to set up a contrast
Immoral men are common
He is established, has a known status

phrases.english: Granted, there, with the girl,
immoral men are common.
But here, even if he is established as one looking for a forgery,
are all the Jewish people established as forgers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison set up in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between the girl who propositioned two men and the man who asked two men to forge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The girl can easily find another willing partner. The lender cannot easily find a willing forger, so there is no reason to assume the document is forged.

steps.title: He may have forged it himself
steps.stepSummary: Since he was actively chasing a forgery, we suspect he forged and wrote the document himself. He does not need anyone else's help.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: since he is chasing after a forgery, say that he forged it and wrote it himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The lender did not need another person to agree to forge, because he could have done it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the forgery needed someone else's help. But a man this eager to forge could simply have written the fake himself. So the document is suspect, just like the girl, and the comparison stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Chasing after, seeking, a forgery
He actually forged it

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's tainted document is one whose owner was seen by two witnesses trying to get it forged. Since he may have forged it himself, he cannot collect with it, just like the girl with a bad reputation gets no קנס.

phrases.english: Here too:
since he is actively seeking a forgery,
say that he forged it and wrote it himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי כֵּיוָן דְּקָא מְהַדַּר אַזִּיּוּפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the needed help is not really needed: he could forge alone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A forgery needs another person's help, and most people are honest.
steps.terutzMaskana: He could have forged it himself, so the document is suspect and cannot be used to collect.

steps.title: New משנה: freed convert, captive or maidservant get no fine
steps.stepSummary: A convert, a captive, or a maidservant who became free after age three and one day gets no קנס if she is raped or seduced.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these get no fine: one who has relations with a convert, a captive, or a maidservant who were redeemed, converted, or freed when older than three years and one day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It lists girls whose father gets no קנס, beginning with girls who came into the Jewish people after age three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fine is paid for a virgin. Girls who lived as non-Jews or captives past age three and one day are presumed not to be virgins. So the attacker pays no fine.

keyTerms.meaning: The fixed fine paid by a rapist or seducer
A female convert
A woman taken captive
A non-Jewish maidservant
Three years and one day, the age after which relations count

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are the girls who do not get a fine:
one who has relations with a convert,
or with a captive, or with a maidservant,
who were redeemed, converted, or freed,
phrases.notes: These three verbs go with the three women in a different order: the captive was redeemed, the convert converted, the maidservant was freed.

phrases.aramaic: יְתֵירוֹת עַל בְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: when older than three years and one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A convert, captive, or maidservant who joined or became free after age three and one day gets no קנס.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a redeemed captive keeps her status
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a redeemed captive is still presumed to be untouched, even if she is grown.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: a captive who was redeemed remains in her holy status, even though she is grown.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first part of the משנה about the captive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion assumed a captive was violated. רבי יהודה does not assume this, so she keeps her status as a virgin. That means she would get a קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: Who was redeemed, ransomed from captivity
In her holy status, still presumed untouched

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
a captive who was redeemed
remains in her state of sanctity,
even though she is an adult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 16 about the captive.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A redeemed captive keeps her presumed status even as an adult.

steps.title: Close relatives: death penalty means no fine
steps.stepSummary: One who has relations with close relatives that carry a court death penalty pays no קנס. A person liable to death does not pay money.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has relations with his daughter, his daughter's daughter, his son's daughter, his wife's daughter, her son's daughter, or her daughter's daughter pays no fine. This is because he is liable to death by the court, and anyone liable to death does not pay money, as it says: 'And if there is no harm, he shall surely be fined.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list. It adds relatives whose relations carry a court death penalty, so no fine is paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason here is different from step 16. These girls may well be virgins. But when one act brings both death and a money payment, only the harsher punishment applies. The פסוק shows that money is paid only when there is no death penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable with his life, deserving the death penalty
Carried out by the court
Harm, here meaning death

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the general rule that one who is liable to death does not also pay money. It appears in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.aramaic: הַבָּא עַל בִּתּוֹ, עַל בַּת בִּתּוֹ,
phrases.english: One who has relations with his daughter, with his daughter's daughter,

phrases.aramaic: עַל בַּת בְּנוֹ, עַל בַּת אִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: with his son's daughter, with his wife's daughter,

phrases.aramaic: עַל בַּת בְּנָהּ, עַל בַּת בִּתָּהּ —
phrases.english: with her son's daughter, or with her daughter's daughter:
phrases.notes: 'Her' means his wife, so these are his wife's granddaughters.

phrases.english: they do not get a fine,
because he is liable with his life,
since their death penalty is carried out by the court.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמִּתְחַיֵּיב בְּנַפְשׁוֹ אֵין מְשַׁלֵּם מָמוֹן,
phrases.english: And anyone who is liable to death does not pay money,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאִם לֹא יִהְיֶה אָסוֹן עָנוֹשׁ יֵעָנֵשׁ״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'And if there is no harm, he shall surely be fined.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּא עַל בִּתּוֹ עַל בַּת בִּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list with a new group and a new reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations that carry a court death penalty bring no קנס, because one liable to death does not pay money.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: רבי יהודה and רבי דוסא hold the same view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי יהודה's view on the captive matches the view of רבי דוסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי יהודה and רבי דוסא said the same thing. רבי יהודה's view is what we just said in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבי יוחנן links רבי יהודה's opinion to another תנא's opinion, and the next step will bring רבי דוסא's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's view is already known from the משנה, where a redeemed captive keeps her status. רבי יוחנן now says רבי דוסא agrees. The next step shows where רבי דוסא says this.

keyTerms.meaning: One and the same thing, the same opinion
What we said, referring back to the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Dosa
said one and the same thing.
Rabbi Yehuda's view is what we said in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי דּוֹסָא אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of רבי יהודה's view from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה and רבי דוסא share the same view about a redeemed captive.

steps.title: רבי דוסא: a redeemed captive may eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי דוסא lets a redeemed captive eat תרומה. He assumes her captor only took small liberties with her and did not have relations with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא's view is taught in a ברייתא: a captive may eat תרומה, these are the words of רבי דוסא. רבי דוסא said: what did this Arab do to her? Just because he squeezed between her breasts, did he make her unfit for כהונה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows רבי דוסא's view, so we can see why רבי יוחנן says it matches רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating תרומה requires that a כהן's wife or daughter was not violated. רבי דוסא assumes the captor only fondled her and did not have relations with her. That is the same assumption רבי יהודה makes in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion given to a כהן, eaten only by those in his household who are fit
This Arab, the captor
He squeezed, fondled
Made her unfit for the priesthood

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה and רבי דוסא both assume a captive was not violated. So she keeps her status: she gets a קנס, according to רבי יהודה, and she may eat תרומה, according to רבי דוסא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa's view is as taught in a ברייתא:
A redeemed captive may eat תרומה,
these are the words of Rabbi Dosa.
Rabbi Dosa said:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עָשָׂה לָהּ עַרְבִי הַלָּז?
phrases.english: And what did this Arab do to her?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמִּיעֵךְ לָהּ בֵּין דַּדֶּיהָ,
phrases.english: And just because he squeezed between her breasts,
did he make her unfit for the priesthood?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא דְּתַנְיָא שְׁבוּיָה אוֹכֶלֶת בִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי דוסא's half of רבי יוחנן's statement in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי דוסא agrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי דוסא permits a redeemed captive to eat תרומה, assuming the captor did not have relations with her.

steps.title: רבה: רבי יהודה may only be lenient so a sinner won't profit
steps.stepSummary: רבה says רבי יהודה might not really agree with רבי דוסא. רבי יהודה may be lenient about קנס only so the attacker does not gain from his sin. About תרומה, he may agree with the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Maybe they do not hold the same view. רבי יהודה only said this here, so that the sinner will not profit. But there, with תרומה, he holds like the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back on רבי יוחנן's claim from step 19 that רבי יהודה and רבי דוסא hold the same view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's lenient ruling about the captive in the קנס case may come from a special reason. If the attacker were exempt, he would profit from his sin. That reason does not apply to תרומה, so there רבי יהודה could be strict like the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Maybe that is not so
He only said it in this case (and not in other cases)
So that the sinner will not profit
He holds like the Rabbis

phrases.english: Rabba said: Perhaps that is not so,
phrases.notes: He is pushing back on רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי יהודה and רבי דוסא agree.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָכָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only said his view here,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the קנס case, where a man attacked a girl who had been a captive.

phrases.english: so that the sinner will not profit?
But there, he holds like the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: "There" means eating תרומה, the case of רבי דוסא from step 20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison of רבי יהודה and רבי דוסא that was made in step 19 and supported in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי יהודה and רבי דוסא hold the same view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה's leniency may come from a reason that applies only to קנס: keeping the sinner from profiting.

steps.title: Second way: רבי דוסא may only be lenient about rabbinic תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives a second way to separate the two views. רבי דוסא may be lenient only because תרומה today is a rabbinic law. For a Torah-level קנס, he may agree with the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: Rabbi Dosa only said his view there, about rabbinic תרומה. But for קנס, which is from the Torah, he holds like the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה offers a second, different reason why the two views may not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the difference comes from רבי דוסא's side. תרומה today is only דרבנן, so being lenient there is easier. A קנס is דאורייתא, so for קנס רבי דוסא might be strict like the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; another possibility
תרומה whose obligation today is rabbinic
A fine required by Torah law

phrases.english: Alternatively:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי דּוֹסָא הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa only said his view there,
with regard to rabbinic תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל קְנָס דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא — כְּרַבָּנַן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: But regarding a Torah-level קנס, he holds like the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי דּוֹסָא הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second way to reject the same comparison. This time the distinction comes from רבי דוסא's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי יהודה and רבי דוסא hold the same view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי דוסא's leniency may apply only to rabbinic matters, not to a Torah-level קנס.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה gives two ways to separate the views: (1) רבי יהודה is lenient only to keep a sinner from profiting; (2) רבי דוסא is lenient only about rabbinic תרומה.

steps.title: אביי: רבי יהודה is also lenient where no sinner is involved
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה's first idea. In a ברייתא, רבי יהודה gives a former captive the full כתובה of a בתולה. There is no sinner there who could profit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is רבי יהודה's reason here really so that the sinner will not profit? But it was taught that רבי יהודה says: A woman who was taken captive keeps her holy status. Even if she was ten years old, her כתובה is two hundred. And there, what sinner could profit?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's first distinction from step 21 using another ruling of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said רבי יהודה is lenient only to stop a sinner from gaining. But in the כתובה case, nobody sinned, and רבי יהודה is still lenient. So it seems he truly believes a captive keeps her presumed purity.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא
In her holy state; still presumed pure
Her כתובה is two hundred זוז, the amount for a בתולה

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And is Rabbi Yehuda's reason here
really so that the sinner will not profit?
But it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A captive woman who was taken captive remains in her holy status,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בַּת עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים — כְּתוּבָּתָהּ מָאתַיִם.
phrases.english: even if she was ten years old, her כתובה is two hundred.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתָם מַאי ״שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא חוֹטֵא נִשְׂכָּר״ אִיכָּא?
phrases.english: And there, what "so the sinner won't profit" is there?
phrases.notes: A כתובה is just about marriage. No one did anything wrong, so no sinner could gain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first distinction רבה gave in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי יהודה is lenient only so that a sinner will not profit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה is also lenient in the כתובה case, where there is no sinner. So the sinner reason cannot explain his view.

steps.title: Answer: there too, there is a special reason, so men won't avoid marrying her
steps.stepSummary: The answer: in the כתובה case, רבי יהודה also has a practical reason. If she got a smaller כתובה, men might avoid marrying her.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, maybe men would hold back and not marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by giving רבי יהודה a different practical reason in the כתובה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that רבי יהודה's leniency always comes from a practical concern, not from a real belief that she is pure. In the קנס case the concern is that the sinner would profit. In the כתובה case the concern is that men would refuse to marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: They would hold back; refrain
They would marry her

phrases.english: There too,
perhaps men would hold back and not marry her.
phrases.notes: If her כתובה were smaller, it would look like she was violated, and men might stay away from her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי, דִּלְמָא מִימַּנְעִי וְלָא נָסְבִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different practical reason that applies to the second case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה is lenient in the כתובה case only because he truly holds that a captive stays pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is lenient there for a practical reason too: so men will not avoid marrying her.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really hold a captive keeps her purity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה really holds that a captive stays pure. In another ברייתא, רבי יהודה says a captive may not be married in either case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold that she remains in her holy status? But it was taught: One who redeems a captive may marry her. One who testifies about her may not marry her. רבי יהודה says: Either way, he may not marry her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge: another ברייתא shows רבי יהודה being strict with a captive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 and the ברייתא in step 23, רבי יהודה treats a captive as pure. But here he forbids a כהן to marry her in every case, which suggests he worries she was violated. These two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: One who redeems (buys the freedom of) a captive woman
He testifies about her (that she was not violated)
Either way; in both cases

steps.confusionAlert: Steps 26-27 first take a side trip to clear up a difficulty inside the ברייתא itself. The גמרא returns to this question in step 28, and steps 29-30 answer it.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda really hold that she remains in her holy status?
But it was taught: One who redeems a captive may marry her.
phrases.notes: This is talking even about a כהן, who may not marry a woman who was violated.

phrases.english: If he testifies about her, he may not marry her.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ לֹא יִשָּׂאֶנָּה!
phrases.english: Either way, he may not marry her!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בִּקְדוּשְׁתַּהּ קָיְימָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against the basic idea that רבי יהודה treats a captive as pure.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that רבי יהודה holds a captive keeps her presumed purity.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this ברייתא, רבי יהודה forbids marrying her in every case. That shows he suspects she was violated.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: Before dealing with רבי יהודה, the גמרא notices a problem inside the ברייתא. If a redeemer may marry her, how could adding testimony make it forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult. You said: One who redeems a captive may marry her. Then it taught: If he testifies about her, he may not marry her. Because he testifies about her, he may not marry her?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the main question to point out that the first part of the ברייתא seems to make no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading the ברייתא simply, a man who redeems her may marry her. A man who redeems her and also says she is pure would then be forbidden. That is backwards, because his testimony should only help her.

keyTerms.meaning: This source itself is difficult
And then it went on to teach

phrases.english: This ברייתא itself is difficult:
You said: One who redeems a captive may marry her,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר תְּנָא: מֵעִיד בָּהּ — לֹא יִשָּׂאֶנָּה.
phrases.english: and then it taught: If he testifies about her, he may not marry her.
Just because he testifies about her, he may not marry her?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first part of the ברייתא (the view of the תנא קמא).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read simply, the ruling is backwards: testimony that she is pure should not make it forbidden to marry her.

steps.title: Answer: redeeming plus testifying is allowed; testifying alone is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the ברייתא's real meaning. If he redeemed her and testifies, he may marry her. If he only testifies, without redeeming her, he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. This is what it means: One who redeems a captive and testifies about her may marry her. If he only testifies about her, he may not marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the side difficulty by reading the ברייתא as two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases include testimony. The difference is whether the man also redeemed her. Only the man who both redeemed her and testified may marry her. Someone who just testifies, with nothing to back up his word, may not marry her. Now the ברייתא makes sense, and the larger question about רבי יהודה is still waiting for an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult
This is what it means
Just like that; with nothing more

phrases.english: This is not difficult. This is what it means:

phrases.aramaic: הַפּוֹדֶה אֶת הַשְּׁבוּיָה וּמֵעִיד בָּהּ — יִשָּׂאֶנָּה,
phrases.english: One who redeems a captive and testifies about her may marry her,
but if he merely testifies about her, he may not marry her.
phrases.notes: כְּדִי means he testified without redeeming her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the side difficulty raised in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the ברייתא as describing two different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא contrasts redeeming (allowed) with testifying (forbidden).
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases include testimony. Redeeming together with testifying is allowed; testifying alone is not.
steps.whatToRemember: In the ברייתא, a man who redeemed a captive and testifies she is pure may marry her, but a man who only testifies may not. The question of how רבי יהודה can forbid her in both cases comes back in step 28 and is answered in steps 29-30.

steps.title: Back to the question on רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Now that the ברייתא's wording is clear, the גמרא repeats its challenge: this ברייתא still contradicts רבי יהודה's other view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, this is a problem for רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the question from step 25. The side issue about the ברייתא's wording is settled, but רבי יהודה still seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 explained the ruling of the רבנן in the ברייתא. Even so, רבי יהודה's words there, that she may not be married in either case, suggest a captive is not presumed pure. That clashes with his ruling that a former captive gets the full כתובה of a בתולה.

keyTerms.meaning: in any case; either way
it is difficult; this is a problem

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult for Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the challenge of step 25 after the side question of steps 26-27 has been settled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In one ברייתא רבי יהודה treats a captive as pure (full כתובה). In the other he forbids marrying her even with testimony, which suggests he does not presume she is pure.

steps.title: רב פפא changes the wording of רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says to read the ברייתא differently: רבי יהודה actually permits marrying her in both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Say it this way. רבי יהודה says: in both cases he may marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the contradiction by changing the words of the ברייתא. רבי יהודה becomes lenient in both cases instead of strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this change, רבי יהודה always treats a captive as presumed pure, just as in the כתובה ruling. So the redeemer may marry her, and so may the man who only testifies. The contradiction disappears because רבי יהודה is lenient in both ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: say it as; read it as (the wording is being changed)
either way; in both cases
he may marry her

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Say instead:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Both in this case and in that case he may marry her.
phrases.notes: "Both cases" means a redeemer who testifies and a man who only testifies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28 by changing the text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה forbids marrying her either way, which contradicts his view that a captive is presumed pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read the ברייתא so that רבי יהודה permits her either way. He is consistently lenient.

steps.title: רב הונא: רבי יהודה was arguing with the רבנן on their own terms
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע keeps the ברייתא as written. He explains that רבי יהודה was showing the רבנן where their own logic should lead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says: Really, keep it as it is taught. רבי יהודה was speaking to the רבנן according to their view. He told them: "In my view, he may marry her either way. But in your view, he should not be allowed to marry her either way!"
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a second answer that does not change any words. רבי יהודה's strict line is not his own ruling. It is an argument against the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה himself holds that a captive is presumed pure, so for him she is permitted in every case. But the רבנן worry that she may have been violated. רבי יהודה tells them that if they really worry, even a redeemer's testimony should not help, and she should be forbidden in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: really, keep it as it was taught (no change to the wording)
according to their words or view
according to me; in my view
according to you (plural); in your view
it should be

steps.confusionAlert: The line "in both cases he may not marry her" is NOT רבי יהודה's own ruling. It is what he says the רבנן ought to hold if they follow their own logic.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, says:
Actually, it is as it was taught,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda was speaking to them according to the words of the Rabbis:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי — בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ יִשָּׂאֶנָּה,
phrases.english: According to me, both in this case and in that case he may marry her,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְדִידְכוּ — בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
phrases.english: but according to you, both in this case and in that case
it should be that he may not marry her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of step 28 that keeps the text instead of changing it as רב פפא did.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the statement is an argument against the other side's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's words "he may not marry her either way" are his own ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: These words show what follows from the רבנן's logic. רבי יהודה himself permits her either way.

steps.title: How the רבנן defend telling the two cases apart
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain why a redeemer who testifies is believed: no one throws away money for nothing. A man who only testifies is not believed, because he may want to marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? A man who redeems a captive and testifies about her may marry her, because a person does not throw away money for nothing. If he only testifies about her, he may not marry her, because maybe he has his eye on her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן would answer רבי יהודה's argument, then gives their reasoning. Paying the ransom makes the redeemer believable. A plain witness has a reason to lie.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said the רבנן should forbid her in both cases. The רבנן answer that the cases are different. A man would not pay a ransom for a woman he planned to marry unless he was sure she was pure, so his payment backs up his testimony. A man who only testifies has paid nothing, so he may be lying to make the marriage possible.

keyTerms.meaning: one who redeems or pays ransom
testifies
a person does not throw away money for nothing
he set his eyes on her (he wants to marry her)

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן tell the cases apart. The redeemer's money backs up his testimony, but a plain witness who wants to marry her is suspect. רבי יהודה presumes a captive is pure anyway. Two answers explain his stricter-sounding line: רב פפא changes the wording, and רב הונא says it was an argument against the רבנן.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means: how do the רבנן answer רבי יהודה's argument that they should forbid her in both cases?

phrases.aramaic: הַפּוֹדֶה אֶת הַשְּׁבוּיָה וּמֵעִיד בָּהּ יִשָּׂאֶנָּה —
phrases.english: One who redeems the captive woman and testifies about her may marry her,
since a person does not throw away money for nothing.
If he merely testifies about her, he may not marry her,
lest he has set his eyes on her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה's argument from step 30 by giving the רבנן's reason for treating the two cases differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling the cases apart based on believability
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the רבנן worry that she was violated, no testimony should permit her, as רבי יהודה argued.
steps.terutzMaskana: Paying the ransom proves the redeemer is sincere. Without it, a witness who wants to marry her is suspected of lying.

steps.title: A new contradiction is introduced
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל is about to present a contradiction to רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא בר שמואל raised a contradiction before רב יוסף:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a new challenge, and the actual contradiction comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רָמֵי means someone is setting two sources against each other. Here it only tells us who asked and whom he asked. The two clashing sources have not been quoted yet.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised a contradiction to him (set two sources against each other)

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
phrases.english: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel raised a contradiction
before Rav Yosef:
